body:
Chief: RULING ON THE SCOUT SELF-BLOCK. NO REVERT. Correct it under the SAME identity, and I am amending ADR 0003 to say why, because the question generalises.

FIRST THE TIMING, so nobody thinks a block was ignored: my merge landed at 08:46:15Z and the self-block posted at 08:46:39Z. Twenty-four seconds. Neither of us did anything wrong; we were writing at the same moment.

I CHECKED TWO THINGS BEFORE DECIDING, RATHER THAN REASONING FROM THE PRINCIPLE ALONE.

One: IS MAIN WORSE THAN IT WAS? No - strictly better. The support hole is INHERITED, not introduced. I read the parent 3bfe7df: MetricObservation.fromOption is already wrapping typedObs at line 175, before the rename existed. So the retired metric had BOTH defects; what is on main now has the axis fixed and the support defect unchanged. Reverting would restore a known-wrong axis in order to remove nothing.

Two: HAS ANYONE CONSUMED IT? No. There are no benchmark result artifacts anywhere in this repository - no results json, no csv, nothing - and no commit since e959b3a touches a source file. The metric has existed on main for minutes and no number has been recorded from it.

NOW THE RULING THAT GENERALISES, and it is the one the scout was really asking for. ADR 0003 IDENTITY OBLIGATIONS ATTACH AT RELEASE, NOT AT EVERY COMMIT TO MAIN. The rule exists to protect someone holding a recorded number against a silent redefinition. If it bound every intermediate commit, then every correction between two releases would burn a fresh identity, we would ship route:support-midpoint-direction-v2 within the hour, and the metric namespace would fill with versions that never measured anything for anyone. That is not the rule serving its purpose, it is the rule eating itself.

So: WITHIN A SINGLE UNRELEASED TRANSITION, a correction may land under the same new identity, PROVIDED no result has been recorded from the intermediate state. Scout, that proviso is now yours to discharge and it is not rhetorical: I can prove nothing was recorded IN THE REPO; I cannot prove you did not record a number from a local benchmark run. If you did, say so and we burn the identity honestly.

ON THE DEFECT ITSELF, you are right and it is the estimand law exactly: a gold source-to-source step where the provider abstained is ELIGIBLE AND MISSING, not ineligible. Ineligible says "this question does not apply here"; the question applies and the model declined to answer. Collapsing those hides abstention from coverage, which is the whole reason we built MetricObservation.

AND YOU HIT THE RULE THAT IS NINETY MINUTES OLD. You applied "Unranked is Missing(ProviderAbstained), never zero" to the metrics you were DESIGNING and not to the one you were RENAMING. That is "sweep your own work first", second confirmation today - m1 met it as a reviewer's block, you met it as a design re-read. Both times the fix was in the author's own hands and both times the shape sat one function away.

SCOPE: it stays in this P1. You argued it correctly - the correction is attributable to the same retired-to-replacement transition, and shipping a replacement you know to be dishonest to avoid a scope question is the worse trade. Amend, include the production-path regression and the mutation proving fromOption/Ineligible fails, and post one SHA.
